sentences.zh: 而且他想成为葡萄牙的国王。

sentences.en: So, he's sort of increasingly torn between Portugal and Brazil.
sentences.zh: 所以，他对葡萄牙和巴西的选择可以说是越来越纠结。

sentences.en: In 1831, the sort of tensions that underlie his rule, you know, is he content as emperor of Brazil?
sentences.zh: 在1831年，他统治之下的那种潜在紧张局势，你知道的，他作为一个巴西皇帝满足吗？

sentences.en: Or does he really ultimately want to go back to Portugal and claim the throne of Portugal?
sentences.zh: 还是说他最终真的想回到葡萄牙去宣称葡萄牙的王位？

sentences.en: These come out in the open.
sentences.zh: 这些矛盾都公开化了。

sentences.en: There are a lot of liberals.
sentences.zh: 有许许多多的自由派人士。

sentences.en: This is among the elite, the sort of elite in cities like Rio.
sentences.zh: 这发生在精英阶层中，比如里约热内卢等城市的精英。

sentences.en: People who are reading newspapers and kind of go into salons and things like that, who kind of chafe a little bit at the idea of an absolute monarch.
sentences.zh: 那些阅读报纸、出入沙龙之类场所的人，对专制君主的理念多多少少有些不耐烦。

sentences.en: Like, they sort of take to the streets and they start sort of shouting, long live the constitution, as people tend to do in the early years of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们走上街头，开始高喊“宪法万岁”，就像19世纪初人们常常做的那样。

sentences.en: There's a thing called the Night of the Bottles, where people are all throwing bottles at each other.
sentences.zh: 当时发生了一件被称为“酒瓶之夜”的事情，大家都在互相扔瓶子。

sentences.en: Yeah, people are throwing bottles at each other.
sentences.zh: 是的，人们在互相扔瓶子。

sentences.en: I assume empty bottles rather than, I mean, it would seem utterly wasteful to be throwing bottles of wine or something at each other.
sentences.zh: 我猜是空瓶子吧，我的意思是，如果拿一瓶瓶的葡萄酒之类的东西互相扔，那可真是太浪费了。

sentences.en: Yeah, that would be a waste, wouldn't it?
sentences.zh: 对啊，那确实是浪费，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it would be a terrible waste.
sentences.zh: 对，那将是极大的浪费。

sentences.en: And there's a sort of great groundswell of opinion against Don Pedro I.
sentences.zh: 反对佩德罗一世的强大民意浪潮涌现了出来。

sentences.en: He says, right, I'm going to abdicate.
sentences.zh: 他说，好勒，我要退位了。

sentences.en: So he abdicates.
sentences.zh: 于是他退位了。

sentences.en: And he flounces off to Portugal, does he?
sentences.zh: 然后他气冲冲地去了葡萄牙，是吗？

sentences.en: And he flounces off to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 然后他气冲冲地去了葡萄牙。

sentences.en: So he abdicates.
sentences.zh: 所以他退位了。

sentences.en: He says, my son is now the emperor, even though his son is six, five and a half.
sentences.zh: 他说，我儿子现在是皇帝了，尽管他儿子才六岁，五岁半。

sentences.en: Six?
sentences.zh: 六岁？

sentences.en: He's abdicated.
sentences.zh: 他退位了。

sentences.en: That's very irresponsible.
sentences.zh: 这太不负责任了。

sentences.en: Five and a half.
sentences.zh: 五岁半。

sentences.en: He says, I'm off.
sentences.zh: 他说，我走了。

sentences.en: I'm out of here.
sentences.zh: 我离开这儿了。

sentences.en: I'm going off to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 我要去葡萄牙了。

sentences.en: So he does go off to Portugal.
sentences.zh: 于是他真的去了葡萄牙。

sentences.en: He fights the civil war in Portugal to try and put his daughter on the throne of Portugal.
sentences.zh: 他在葡萄牙打内战，试图把他的女儿扶上葡萄牙的王位。

sentences.en: So what's his plan?
sentences.zh: 那他的计划是什么？

sentences.en: He's going to be the power behind the throne.
sentences.zh: 他打算做王权背后的操纵者。

sentences.en: The Portuguese have made it clear they don't want him as king.
sentences.zh: 葡萄牙人已经明确表示不希望他当国王。

sentences.en: But he thinks, I'll put my daughter on the throne and I'll be the big man.
sentences.zh: 但他心想，我要把女儿扶上王位，而我来当幕后大佬。

sentences.en: And he dies of tuberculosis in the hour of his victory, Tom.
sentences.zh: 结果他在胜利的时刻因结核病去世了，汤姆。

sentences.en: Oh, that's sad.
sentences.zh: 哦，那真令人难过。

sentences.en: But interestingly, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，重点来了。

sentences.en: Here's a sort of portent of the future.
sentences.zh: 这里有一个未来的某种预兆。

sentences.en: Don Pedro I, who we described as useless.
sentences.zh: 佩德罗一世，我们之前说他一无是处。

sentences.en: On his deathbed, he writes an open letter to the people of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 在临终病榻上，他给巴西人民写了一封公开信。

sentences.en: So he hasn't forgotten about Brazil, which is nice.
sentences.zh: 所以他没有忘记巴西，这挺好的。

sentences.en: Okay, that's good.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这倒不错。

sentences.en: And in the open letter, he says, slavery is an evil and an attack against the rights and dignity of the human species.
sentences.zh: 在这封公开信中，他说，奴隶制是一种罪恶，是对人类尊严和权利的侵犯。

sentences.en: But its consequences are less harmful to those who suffer in captivity than to the nation whose laws allow slavery.
sentences.zh: 但其后果对身处枷锁中的受害者造成的损害，其实小于对那些容许奴隶制的国家的损害。

sentences.en: It is cancer that devours its morality.
sentences.zh: 它就像毒瘤一样吞噬着国家的道德。

sentences.en: So he's sort of pinning his saying, you know, the monarchy should not be in favor of slavery and slavery is very bad.
sentences.zh: 所以他明确表态说，君主制不应该支持奴隶制，奴隶制是非常糟糕的。

sentences.en: Well, I'm sure the slaves are happy about that, but I'm not entirely sure they'd agree with him that they're better off than their owners.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我相信奴隶们对此会很高兴，但我不太确定他们会同意自己比主人过得更好的说法。

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，完全正确。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Who's the real victim here?
sentences.zh: 谁才是真正的受害者？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: So anyway, Don Pedro I is dead.
sentences.zh: 总之，佩德罗一世去世了。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, back in Brazil, the Brazilians are having to get used to their second emperor, who is not yet six years old.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，在巴西，巴西人不得不习惯他们的第二位皇帝，他还不到六岁。

sentences.en: So poor little Don Pedro II, they bring him onto a balcony in Rio.
sentences.zh: 所以可怜的小佩德罗二世，他们把他带到了里约的一处阳台上。

sentences.en: He's so small, he can't kind of look over the balustrade.
sentences.zh: 他太矮了，根本看不到栏杆外面。

sentences.en: So they put him on a chair and he waves a hanky.
sentences.zh: 于是他们把他放在一张椅子上，让他挥舞手帕。

sentences.en: They get him to wave a hanky to the crowds and everybody cheers and says, hurrah, hurrah, hurrah.
sentences.zh: 他们让他向人群挥手帕，大家欢呼着，喊着乌拉、乌拉、乌拉。

sentences.en: But for him, this is very bad news.
sentences.zh: 但对他来说，这绝对是个大坏消息。

sentences.en: He's sent off to a palace called São Cristóvão with his two sisters, Francisca and Januária.
sentences.zh: 他被送到了一个叫圣克里斯托旺的宫殿，和他的两个姐姐弗兰西斯卡和雅努阿尔娅在一起。

sentences.en: January.
sentences.zh: 雅努阿尔娅。

sentences.en: Great name.
sentences.zh: 好名字。

sentences.en: Great, great name.
sentences.zh: 真是个好名字。

sentences.en: And they basically are just sort of locked in this palace and given endless lessons.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们就被锁在这座宫殿里，接受无穷无尽的课程。

sentences.en: So the Brazilians think it's very important that their future emperor, well, their current emperor, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以巴西人认为他们的未来皇帝——好吧，我想应该是现任皇帝——非常重要。

sentences.en: And what are they teaching him?
sentences.zh: 他们在教他什么？

sentences.en: Lepidopathy?
sentences.zh: 鳞翅目学？

sentences.en: They teach him, well, we know because we have a letter.
sentences.zh: 他们教他……好吧，我们知道，因为我们有一封信。

sentences.en: Botany?
sentences.zh: 植物学？

sentences.en: There are very few sources, actually, Tom, on the life of poor Don Pedro II, because he's locked in his room the whole time.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，其实关于可怜的佩德罗二世一生的资料非常少，因为他整天都被锁在房间里。

sentences.en: So we don't really know.
sentences.zh: 所以我们其实并不太了解。

sentences.en: But he writes a letter to his sister at one point, in 1833, and he says, writing, arithmetic, geography, drawing, French, English, music, and dance divide our time.
sentences.zh: 但在1833年的某个时候，他写信给他的姐姐说：写作、算术、地理、绘画、法语、英语、音乐和舞蹈填满了我们的时间。

sentences.en: We work constantly to acquire knowledge.
sentences.zh: 我们不断学习以获取知识。

sentences.en: And it is only these efforts that mitigate how sorely we miss you during our separation.
sentences.zh: 只有这些努力才能减轻我们分别期间对你刻骨的思念。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 噢。

sentences.en: So he's not really allowed any friends.
sentences.zh: 所以他其实不被允许有任何朋友。

sentences.en: So he's not really learning about rainforests or anything.
sentences.zh: 所以他并没有真正了解雨林之类的事情。

sentences.en: No, no, no.
sentences.zh: 不，不，不。

sentences.en: He's learning European, old world sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 他学的是欧洲旧大陆的那种东西。

sentences.en: So he's sort of locked in his room doing arithmetic all the time.
sentences.zh: 所以他被锁在房间里不停地做算术。

sentences.en: He's pretty miserable.
sentences.zh: 他相当痛苦。

sentences.en: He's pretty unhappy.
sentences.zh: 他非常不快乐。

sentences.en: He's lonely.
sentences.zh: 他很孤独。

sentences.en: He's been separated from his parents.
sentences.zh: 他与父母分离了。

sentences.en: He's kind of shy and he's reclusive.
sentences.zh: 他有点害羞，而且性格孤僻。

sentences.en: So there's the emperor.
sentences.zh: 这就是那位皇帝。

sentences.en: He's the little boy who's the emperor of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他是那个身为巴西皇帝的小男孩。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, Brazil itself is a bit of a, I wouldn't call it a basket case.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，巴西本身有点像个……我不会称之为彻底失败的国家。

sentences.en: That's too harsh.
sentences.zh: 那样太严厉了。

sentences.en: But you asked about slave revolts.
sentences.zh: 但你问到了奴隶起义。

sentences.en: There are an awful lot of slave revolts in the early decades of Brazilian independence.
sentences.zh: 在巴西独立后的头几十年里，发生了非常多的奴隶起义。

sentences.en: So the state of Pernambuco, there's a big revolt called the Cabanada Revolt.
sentences.zh: 所以在伯南布哥州，有一场名为卡巴纳达起义的大规模暴动。

sentences.en: And that's, you've got Brazilian Indians, escaped slaves, squatters, people who've sort of been marginalized and forced out.
sentences.zh: 那是巴西印第安人、逃亡奴隶、擅自占地者以及被边缘化和驱逐的人们的汇聚。

sentences.en: They all come together and they form their own kind of community in the woods.
sentences.zh: 他们聚集在一起，在树林里组成了自己的某种社区。

sentences.en: And they kind of, they form their own army and they're always fighting off the landowners' attempts to kind of put them down.
sentences.zh: 他们组建了自己的军队，不断击退地主们试图镇压他们的企图。

sentences.en: And this is a real theme of 19th century Brazilian history.
sentences.zh: 这是19世纪巴西历史的一个真正的主题。

sentences.en: And how long did they manage to hold out?
sentences.zh: 他们坚持抵抗了多久？

sentences.en: They held out for about four years.
sentences.zh: 他们坚持了大约四年。

sentences.en: I mean, quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，相当长的一段时间了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And this is absolutely the, you know, you see this pattern again and again.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是……你会一次又一次地看到这种模式。

sentences.en: So in the big, huge northern state of Para in the late 1830s, there's another revolt of, again, sort of Indians, slaves and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪30年代末的北部超级大州帕拉，又发生了一场起义，同样是由印第安人、奴隶等发起的。

sentences.en: And their slaves turn against their masters and they whip them and kill them.
sentences.zh: 他们的奴隶背叛了主人，鞭笞并杀害了他们。

sentences.en: And in the cities, there are huge sort of outpourings of hatred against the slaves and the Indians.
sentences.zh: 而在城市里，对奴隶和印第安人的仇恨情绪大规模爆发。

sentences.en: And people say they're evil, they're the forces of the devil.
sentences.zh: 人们说他们是邪恶的，是魔鬼的化身。

sentences.en: You know, this is what happened in Haiti, the Haitian Revolution.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这就是海地发生的事，海地革命。

sentences.en: That will happen here in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 这也会在巴西发生。

sentences.en: The only way to deal with them is by, you know, intense violence and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 对付他们的唯一方法就是……你知道的，采取极其暴力的手段等等。

sentences.en: And there is a colossal amount of violence.
sentences.zh: 而且确实发生了大量的暴力事件。

sentences.en: So in states like Para, I mean, I think something like 100,000 people were killed.
sentences.zh: 所以在帕拉这样的州，我的意思是，我想大概有十万人被杀。

sentences.en: I mean, these are massive, you know, death tolls.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这些都是巨大的死亡人数。

sentences.en: I was about to say utterly unreported in the old world.
sentences.zh: 我正想说，在旧大陆对此完全没有任何报道。

sentences.en: That's not really true.
sentences.zh: 这其实不太对。

sentences.en: But what is true, I suppose, is that they're utterly forgotten today.
sentences.zh: 但我想，真正的事实是它们在今天被彻底遗忘了。

sentences.en: And so in Europe, people aren't even aware that these things happened.
sentences.zh: 所以在欧洲，人们甚至不知道这些事情曾经发生过。

sentences.en: Well, presumably they are in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 嗯，想必在葡萄牙他们是知道的吧。

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm sure people know about it in Portugal.
sentences.zh: 对，我确信在葡萄牙人们知道这件事。

sentences.en: But we know about American history because we speak English.
sentences.zh: 但我们了解美国历史是因为我们说英语。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对的。

sentences.en: I suppose that's true.
sentences.zh: 我想确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, that's the reason.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，原因就在于此。

sentences.en: A slave revolt that would really interest you is in the sort of northeastern state of Baia in 1835.
sentences.zh: 一场真正会让你感兴趣的奴隶起义发生在1835年的东北部巴伊亚州。

sentences.en: The famous city there, which is a huge sort of trading sort of center for the slave trade, Salvador.
sentences.zh: 那里的著名城市萨尔瓦多，是奴隶贸易的一个巨大贸易中心。

sentences.en: So there, there's an Islamic element to the slave revolt.
sentences.zh: 所以在那里，奴隶起义中带有一种伊斯兰教的因素。

sentences.en: Wow, that's unexpected.
sentences.zh: 哇，这真是出乎意料。

sentences.en: So a lot of the African slaves who are being brought to Baia are MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多被带到巴伊亚的非洲奴隶都是穆斯林。

sentences.en: And Islam becomes the kind of the common ground for different groups of slaves so they can unite around their faith.
sentences.zh: 伊斯兰教成了不同奴隶群体之间的共同基础，使他们能够围绕信仰团结起来。

sentences.en: So they wear white tunics, white prayer tunics.
sentences.zh: 所以他们身穿白色的束腰外衣，白色的祈祷服。

sentences.en: They wear amulets inscribed with verses from the Koran when they, when they rise up.
sentences.zh: 当他们起义时，他们佩戴刻有《古兰经》经文的护身符。

sentences.en: And of course, that then means that for the slave owners, it's a religious war.
sentences.zh: 当然，这就意味着对奴隶主来说，这是一场宗教战争。

sentences.en: It's a religious war.
sentences.zh: 这是一场宗教战争。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So again, extremely violent.
sentences.zh: 所以同样地，极其暴力。

sentences.en: When that's put down, 500 people are executed, publicly executed.
sentences.zh: 当起义被平息时，有500人被处决，公开处决。

sentences.en: Are there traces of Islam still in Salvador?
sentences.zh: 萨尔瓦多现在还有伊斯兰教的痕迹吗？

sentences.en: That's a good question, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这是个好问题，汤姆。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I don't know at all.
sentences.zh: 我完全不知道。

sentences.en: Of course, the big story in Brazil has been the rise of Protestant evangelicalism.
sentences.zh: 当然，巴西近年来的大新闻是新教福音派的崛起。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So originally a Catholic country, but- I just wondered whether- But I don't know.
sentences.zh: 所以原本是个天主教国家，但是……我只是想知道是否……但我不知道。

sentences.en: I'd be interested to find out, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我很想去了解一下。

sentences.en: Maybe so if we have Brazilian listeners.
sentences.zh: 如果我们有巴西听众的话，也许他们会知道。

sentences.en: I don't think we ultimately do have many Brazilian listeners, but we do have a few, Tom, because we put out our Brazilian independence episode.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我们最终其实没有多少巴西听众，但确实有几个，汤姆，因为我们发布了巴西独立那一集节目。

sentences.en: Yes, we did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们发过。

sentences.en: So the story about the Portuguese court on Brazil's independence day.
sentences.zh: 也就是关于巴西独立日当天葡萄牙宫廷的故事。

sentences.en: And we had some listeners saying it was actually a complete coincidence, wasn't it?
sentences.zh: 有些听众说这其实完全是个巧合，对吧？

sentences.en: But we pretended it was by design and their Brazilian listeners were very, very excited.
sentences.zh: 但我们假装那是刻意安排的，巴西听众们对此感到非常非常兴奋。

sentences.en: So there's a real sense at the end of the 1830s, anyway, that Brazil is a bit of a sort of, it's in a terrible ferment with all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1830年代末期，无论如何，人们有一种强烈的感受，即巴西正处于某种状态，充斥着各种各样的动荡。

sentences.en: And the elites decide, the way to deal with this is actually, we need to crown the emperor, even though he's still only a teenager.
sentences.zh: 精英们决定，应对这一局面的办法实际上是——我们需要为皇帝加冕，尽管他当时还只是个青少年。

sentences.en: If we put him in charge, he will be a figure around whom everybody can kind of rally.
sentences.zh: 如果我们让他掌权，他将成为一个能让所有人团结在他周围的凝聚核心。

sentences.en: So it's 1841, and he is what?
sentences.zh: 所以那是1841年，他多大了？

sentences.en: He's about to turn 16.
sentences.zh: 他快满16岁了。

sentences.en: And they have this huge coronation ceremony in Rio.
sentences.zh: 他们在里约热内卢举行了一场盛大的加冕典礼。

sentences.en: So all the newspapers sort of say, he is the greatest man of his generation.
sentences.zh: 因此，所有的报纸都说，他是他那一代人中最伟大的人。

sentences.en: He is the new, you know, Charles V or whatever.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是新查理五世之类的人物。

sentences.zh: 而且我想——我觉得巴西皇帝就是住在那里。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that tradition of that library and that kind of tradition of scholarship and interest in the natural world, to a degree, is something that he must be picking up on from that.
sentences.zh: 所以这种图书馆的传统，以及那种对学术和自然界的热爱与传统的某种程度延续，必然是他从那继承来的。

sentences.en: Oh, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对是。

sentences.en: And I think what's really interesting is that he's – so what he's trying to do, is he trying to reproduce the old world in the new?
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得真正有趣的是，他——他到底在做什么呢？他是在新世界里复制旧世界吗？

sentences.en: I mean, not quite.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也不完全是。

sentences.en: He's giving it this spin, this sort of tropical culture and this tropical monarchy.
sentences.zh: 他给它注入了新的特色，这种热带文化和热带君主制。

sentences.en: But he's obviously very – you know, it's very important to Don Pedro II that he creates a Brazilian culture that people will consider alongside, you know, Portuguese, Spanish,
sentences.zh: 但很显然——你知道的，佩德罗二世陛下非常看重的一点是，他要创造一种能与葡萄牙、西班牙相提并论的巴西文化……

sentences.en: French, German, Italian culture or whatever.
sentences.zh: 法国、德国、意大利文化或者诸如此类。

sentences.en: That it's part of the same kind of continuum, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我想，它是同一种连续体的一部分。

sentences.en: And science, he's absolutely passionate about science.
sentences.zh: 至于科学，他是绝对的热爱科学。

sentences.en: He's the first Brazilian photographer because he acquires a kind of very early daguerreotype camera in 1840.
sentences.zh: 他是巴西的第一位摄影师，因为他在1840年获得了一种非常早期的银版照相机。

sentences.en: He sets up a photo laboratory in his palace in São Cristóvão.
sentences.zh: 他在圣克里斯托弗宫设立了一个照相实验室。

sentences.en: He also has a chemistry laboratory and a physics laboratory.
sentences.zh: 他还有一个化学实验室和一个物理实验室。

sentences.en: He has an astronomical observatory.
sentences.zh: 他有一座天文台。

sentences.en: He has a saying that he likes to bring out and bore his courteous with.
sentences.zh: 他有一句口头禅，喜欢拿出来在朝臣面前卖弄。

sentences.en: He says, la science, c'est moi.
sentences.zh: 他说：科学就是我。

sentences.en: Well, Dominic, I'm just reading in the Bodleian that he – apparently there was a meteorite that landed in the Badlands and he sent an expedition to try and find it.
sentences.zh: 好吧，多米尼克，我刚在博德利图书馆看到——据说有颗陨石落在了荒地，然后他派了一支远征队去寻找它。

sentences.en: But that's exactly the kind of thing he did.
sentences.zh: 但这正是他会做的事。

sentences.en: It was a five metric tonne space rock.
sentences.zh: 那是一块重达五公吨的太空岩石。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Did they get it?
sentences.zh: 他们找到了吗？

sentences.en: So it landed in 1784.
sentences.zh: 它是在1784年坠落的。

sentences.en: And so when Pedro II learned about the meteorite, he organised a commission of engineers to relocate it to Rio.
sentences.zh: 所以当佩德罗二世得知这颗陨石的消息后，他组织了一个工程师委员会，将其运到里约热内卢。

sentences.en: And the trek lasted 126 days.
sentences.zh: 这场跋涉持续了126天。

sentences.en: And it was taken to the National Museum, the one with the library.
sentences.zh: 它被送到了国家博物馆，就是那个带图书馆的博物馆。

sentences.en: So there you go.
sentences.zh: 所以你看。

sentences.en: And I'm glad to say that that meteorite was among the objects that were left unscathed by the fire that destroyed the museum.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴地说，那颗陨石是在那场摧毁博物馆的大火中完好无损的藏品之一。

sentences.en: So it survived.
sentences.zh: 所以它幸存了下来。

sentences.en: So that's good news.
sentences.zh: 这是个好消息。

sentences.en: Tom, as somebody who likes science, dinosaurs, all that kind of business, you would love Don Pedro II.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，作为一个喜欢科学、恐龙和诸如此类事物的人，你一定会喜欢佩德罗二世。

sentences.en: He sounds great, great guy.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒，是个绝佳的人选。

sentences.en: He's a man of –
sentences.zh: 他是一个——

sentences.en: I'll tell you what he sounds like.
sentences.zh: 我告诉你他听起来像什么。

sentences.en: He sounds an absolutely ideal subject to be the hero of a magical realist novel.
sentences.zh: 他听起来绝对是魔幻现实主义小说男主角的理想人选。

sentences.en: Yeah, he absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 对，他绝对是。

sentences.en: He absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 他绝对是。

sentences.en: So he's very into literature as well.
sentences.zh: 所以他也非常痴迷文学。

sentences.en: He writes to people like Victor Hugo, to Nietzsche, to Wagner, to all these people.
sentences.zh: 他给维克多·雨果、尼采、瓦格纳以及所有人写信。

sentences.en: You know, they think he's brilliant.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们觉得他才华横溢。

sentences.en: So his reputation in Europe, among sort of European lettered classes, could not be higher.
sentences.zh: 因此他在欧洲文人阶层中的声誉，简直达到了无以复加的地步。

sentences.en: He asked Wagner to write an opera that would be premiered in Rio.
sentences.zh: 他曾请瓦格纳写一部歌剧，在里约热内卢首演。

sentences.en: So would you say he is the Pele of cultured European monarchs?
sentences.zh: 那你觉得他是文化界欧洲君主中的贝利吗？

sentences.en: Very nice, yes.
sentences.zh: 比喻得真好，是的。

sentences.en: He's the Pele, rather than the Neymar, of European-style American monarchs.
sentences.zh: 与其说是欧洲式美洲君主中的内马尔，不如说是贝利。

sentences.en: I think it's fair to say.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这么说很公允。

sentences.en: So, yeah, he asked Wagner to write an opera.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，他邀请瓦格纳写一部歌剧。

sentences.en: Wagner was too busy, so he couldn't.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳太忙了，所以没能写。

sentences.en: However, supposedly, when they did the whole ring cycle at Bayreuth in 1876, Don Pedro II was present.
sentences.zh: 不过据说，1876年在拜罗伊特上演整部《尼伯龙根的指环》时，佩德罗二世就在现场。

sentences.en: We should come on to his European travels in due course.
sentences.zh: 我们随后该聊聊他的欧洲之旅了。

sentences.en: And he sat next to the new emperor of Germany at the premier.
sentences.zh: 首演时他就坐在新任德国皇帝旁边。

sentences.en: So this is not the Kaiser, Tom, friend of the rest is history, great yachting enthusiast and shoe wearer.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这可不是那位凯撒，就是那位“历史由你书写”的朋友、狂热的游艇爱好者兼鞋子佩戴者。

sentences.en: Now, it's his grandfather, Kaiser Wilhelm I, and Don Pedro ruins the opera for everybody by constantly saying to all the other bigwigs, he says, oh,
sentences.zh: 不，这是他的祖父，威廉一世皇帝，佩德罗一路上不停地对其他大人物说，把所有人的歌剧兴致都破坏了，他说，哦，

sentences.en: I'm very familiar with this music.
sentences.zh: 我对这段音乐太熟悉了。

sentences.en: This is the first time you've heard it, but I know it by heart.
sentences.zh: 这是你们第一次听，但我已经烂熟于心了。

sentences.en: I know all about this.
sentences.zh: 我对这一切了如指掌。

sentences.en: You don't need to tell me anything about Wagner.
sentences.zh: 你们不需要跟我讲任何关于瓦格纳的事。

sentences.en: I know Wagner.
sentences.zh: 我懂瓦格纳。

sentences.en: I love Wagner.
sentences.zh: 我爱瓦格纳。

sentences.en: Wagner's my friend and all this kind of thing, which drives everybody else completely, completely mad.
sentences.zh: 瓦格纳是我的朋友，诸如此类的话，这把其他所有人都快折磨疯了。

sentences.en: So, in other words, his reputation is sky high.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他的声誉如日中天。

sentences.en: Brazil itself, they fight a terrible, incredibly bloody war called the War of the Triple Alliance in Paraguay in the 1860s, which, apart from being bloody,
sentences.zh: 至于巴西本土，他们在19世纪60年代打了一场极其可怕、血腥至极的战争，叫做巴拉圭战争（三国同盟战争），除了血腥之外，

sentences.en: it's very useful for Brazil because it creates this sort of image of Brazilian nationalism and of the sort of united fatherland and all this sort of stuff.
sentences.zh: 这对巴西非常有用，因为它塑造了巴西民族主义的形象，以及统一的祖国等等诸如此类的概念。

sentences.en: But obviously, there is this issue of slavery.
sentences.zh: 但显然，这里存在着奴隶制的问题。

sentences.en: Now, let's get to the 1870s.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们把时间推到19世纪70年代。

sentences.en: Brazil has about 10 million people by now, and between 10% and 20% of them, I think, are slaves.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，巴西大约有1000万人口，其中我想有10%到20%是奴隶。

sentences.en: But the sort of the epicenter of slavery has slightly moved because what's changed with Brazil is before we were talking about gold and we're talking about the mining.
sentences.zh: 但奴隶制的中心稍微转移了，因为巴西的变化在于，以前我们谈论的是黄金和采矿。

sentences.en: But the big thing in Brazil now is coffee.
sentences.zh: 但现在巴西最重要的大事是咖啡。

sentences.en: So, coffee is produced in the south of Brazil, and that's where the sort of the epicenter of slavery has really moved to.
sentences.zh: 因此，咖啡产于巴西南部，这也是奴隶制中心真正转移到的地方。

sentences.en: The big landowners are based in the south around Rio and Sao Paulo, and in the big sort of the four southernmost provinces,
sentences.zh: 大土地所有者主要集中在里约和圣保罗南部的四个主要省份，

sentences.en: about just under two-thirds of the population are slaves.
sentences.zh: 那里的绝大多数人口——不到三分之二——都是奴隶。

sentences.en: Now, the emperor himself, Don Pedro II, personally, is not in favor of slavery at all.
sentences.zh: 至于皇帝本人，佩德罗二世，个人而言，他一点也不支持奴隶制。

sentences.en: He never bought slaves.
sentences.zh: 他从不买奴隶。

sentences.en: He inherited 40 slaves, and he set them all free as soon as he could.
sentences.zh: 他继承了40名奴隶，并一有机会就把他们全都释放了。

sentences.en: He would often write to friends, and he would say he doesn't like slavery.
sentences.zh: 他经常写信给朋友，说自己不喜欢奴隶制。

sentences.en: Slavery is a terrible curse on my nation, he would say.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制是我国家的沉重诅咒，他会这样说。

sentences.en: But he was always inhibited from moving against it because he's worried about alienating the elite.
sentences.zh: 但他总是无法采取行动反对它，因为他担心会疏远精英阶层。

sentences.en: He thinks the elite who own the slaves, he depends on them for his power.
sentences.zh: 他认为拥有奴隶的精英阶层是他权力的支柱。

sentences.en: So, Brazil is sort of slowly beginning to change.
sentences.zh: 所以，巴西开始慢慢发生变化。

sentences.en: So, they do things like there's a law of free birth in 1871, which is that basically all children of slaves will be freed.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们出台了一些举措，比如1871年的《自由出生法》，基本上就是所有奴隶生下的孩子都将获得自由。

sentences.en: They have to stay with their mothers until they're eight, and then their owners, the mother's owner, can choose between being compensated by the state then and there,
sentences.zh: 他们必须跟母亲生活到八岁，然后他们的主人，也就是母亲的主人，可以选择当时就接受国家的补偿，

sentences.en: and their child is set free at the age of eight, or they can continue to use the child's services until the child turns 21.
sentences.zh: 然后孩子在八岁时获得自由，或者他们可以继续利用该孩子的劳动力，直到孩子满21岁。

sentences.en: So, this is hardly, you know, kind of overnight abolition.
sentences.zh: 所以，这根本谈不上什么一夜之间废除奴隶制。

sentences.en: But even so, it begins to alienate the big kind of coffee elites, the slave owners, because they start to think,
sentences.zh: 即便如此，这也开始疏远那些大型咖啡精英、奴隶主，因为他们开始觉得，

sentences.en: well, if the government can do this, the monarch is not to be trusted.
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果政府能这样做，君主就不可信了。

sentences.en: The monarch is going to end up abolishing slavery completely.
sentences.zh: 君主最终会彻底废除奴隶制。

sentences.en: This is all a very bad thing.
sentences.zh: 这可真不是件好事。

sentences.en: So, what you get in the 1870s is something that I think a lot of listeners may consider, may find a bit weird,
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪70年代，你会发现一件很多听众可能会觉得有点奇怪的事，

sentences.en: which is that what you'd call the kind of liberal elite, i.e. the people who read newspapers, who go to the opera,
sentences.zh: 那就是所谓的大众口中的自由派精英，也就是那些读报纸、去歌剧院的人，

sentences.en: who, you know, are sophisticated, you know, people of the world, people who are well-traveled.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他们是老练的、见多识广的世界人，是游历广泛的人。

sentences.en: These people start to flirt with republicanism and become interested in republicanism because they equate republicanism with the defense of slavery.
sentences.zh: 这些人开始涉足共和主义并对共和主义产生兴趣，因为他们把共和主义与维护奴隶制等同起来。

sentences.en: So, in other words, something that you might think of as very progressive becomes identified with a cause that could hardly be more reactionary.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你本以为非常进步的东西，却被和一个极其反动的目标联系在了一起。

sentences.en: So, there's this sort of sense in the 1870s that for all his amazing scientific stuff, meteorite, interfering with meteorites.
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪70年代有一种感觉，尽管他做了那么多惊人的科学壮举，陨石，插手陨石事务。

sentences.en: Sourcing it, yeah.
sentences.zh: 寻找陨石，对。

sentences.en: Yeah, being a fan of Wagner, all this kind of stuff, that the emperor is losing support among the very people that he really most needs to keep his regime going.
sentences.zh: 是的，作为瓦格纳的粉丝，诸如此类，但皇帝正在失去那些维系他政权最需要的人的支持。

sentences.en: But do the slaves not love him?
sentences.zh: 难道奴隶们不爱他吗？

sentences.en: Well, yeah, the slaves do, as we'll discover, the slaves do quite like the emperor because they see him as the sort of face of the abolitionist movement,
sentences.zh: 嗯，对，奴隶们确实爱他，正如我们接下来会发现的那样，奴隶们相当喜欢皇帝，因为他们视他为废奴运动的代言人，

sentences.en: which is perhaps a slight misreading of it because he doesn't really do that much to encourage abolition.
sentences.zh: 这或许有点误读，因为他并没有做太多实质性的事情来鼓励废奴。

sentences.en: So, you start to get mockery of Pedro II.
sentences.zh: 所以，人们开始嘲笑佩德罗二世。

sentences.en: People, they have some very strange names for him, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，人们给他取了一些非常奇怪的名字。

sentences.en: His opponents call him Pedro Banana.
sentences.zh: 他的反对者叫他“香蕉佩德罗”。

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Seems very harsh.
sentences.zh: 听起来很刻薄。

sentences.en: Well, I say his head is very long.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为我说他的头很长。

sentences.en: He has a very long head.
sentences.zh: 他长着一个非常长的脑袋。

sentences.en: He looks like a banana.
sentences.zh: 他看起来像根香蕉。

sentences.en: Right, okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧，原来如此。

sentences.en: Maybe his sort of Habsburg blood or something like that.
sentences.zh: 也许是他那哈布斯堡家族的血统之类的原因吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: They also call him Pedro.
sentences.zh: 他们还叫他佩德罗。

sentences.en: They used to call Pericles the squid.
sentences.zh: 他们以前管伯里克利叫乌贼。

sentences.en: The squid.
sentences.zh: 乌贼。

sentences.en: They also call him Pedro the cashew.
sentences.zh: 他们还叫他“腰果佩德罗”。

sentences.en: Would you rather be a cashew or a banana, Tom?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你愿意当腰果还是香蕉？

sentences.en: I think cashew.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当腰果吧。

sentences.en: I think a cashew as well.
sentences.zh: 我也觉得当腰果好。

sentences.en: I think I'd much rather be likened to a cashew.
sentences.zh: 我想我更愿意被比作腰果。

sentences.en: I think a banana is just undecorous, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我觉得把人比作香蕉未免太不雅观了吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: If you're going to be likened to a fruit of any kind.
sentences.zh: 如果你非得被比作某种水果的话。

sentences.en: Louis Philippe.
sentences.zh: 路易·菲利普。

sentences.en: In France, he's likened to a pear.
sentences.zh: 在法国，他被比作一个梨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And Chiang Kai-shek was likened to a peanut, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 蒋介石被比作花生，对吧？

sentences.en: Was he?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: By General Sitwell.
sentences.zh: 史迪威将军说的。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Of course he was.
sentences.zh: 当然是他。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: He used to call him a peanut.
sentences.zh: 他以前管他叫花生。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So there's a whole podcast we've done about emperors and nuts.
sentences.zh: 所以我们之前做过一整期关于皇帝和坚果的播客。

sentences.en: Fruit and nut based abuse is.
sentences.zh: 水果和坚果引发的虐待是。

sentences.en: It's a real theme there that we can perhaps run with a bit later on.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个很好的主题，我们可能等会儿还可以接着聊。

sentences.en: It definitely is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So the elites, the sort of liberal elites think that Don Pedro is unsound on slavery.
sentences.zh: 所以精英阶层，也就是那种自由派精英，认为佩德罗二世在废奴问题上态度不够坚决。

sentences.en: They also think he's unsound on travel.
sentences.zh: 他们还认为他在旅行这方面很不靠谱。

sentences.en: Because in the 1870s, he starts to go traveling a lot.
sentences.zh: 因为在19世纪70年代，他开始频繁外出旅行。

sentences.en: And they think this is very bad and very unpatriotic.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得这非常糟糕，而且非常不爱国。

sentences.en: And he should be more interested in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他应该把更多精力放在巴西上。

sentences.en: But he keeps sort of going for these jaunts around Europe.
sentences.zh: 但他却总是在欧洲各地到处闲逛。

sentences.en: So he goes to America.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了美洲。

sentences.en: So Tom, would you believe he is the first ruling monarch to set foot in the United States?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，你敢相信他是第一位踏上美国土地的在位君主吗？

sentences.en: But not the first to set foot in North America, because Maximilian of Mexico, who we did a whole episode on, didn't we?
sentences.zh: 但不是第一位踏上北美土地的，因为我们专门做过一整期节目的墨西哥马克西米利安，对吧？

sentences.en: We did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So when Eunice's S.
sentences.zh: 所以当尤利西斯·S·

sentences.en: Grant opens the World's Fair in Philadelphia in 1876, Don Pedro II is standing by his side.
sentences.zh: 格兰特于1876年在费城开办世界博览会时，佩德罗二世就站在他身旁。

sentences.en: I mean, the World's Fair, he loves all that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，世博会，他可太喜欢这些了。

sentences.en: Science, machines, displays of Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 科学、机器、波斯尼亚的展品。

sentences.en: International travel.
sentences.zh: 国际旅行。

sentences.en: International travel, exactly.
sentences.zh: 国际旅行，没错。

sentences.en: He goes to visit Alexander Graham Bell and allows him to test his first telephone, which is very nice.
sentences.zh: 他去拜访了亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔，并允许他测试自己的第一台电话，这非常棒。
zh_words: 亚历山大·格雷厄姆·贝尔

sentences.en: He goes off to France.
sentences.zh: 他动身去了法国。

sentences.en: He goes to visit Victor Hugo.
sentences.zh: 他去拜访了维克多·雨果。

sentences.en: He visits Victor Hugo at his house.
sentences.zh: 他亲自去雨果的住所拜访了他。

sentences.en: There's a lovely story here, Tom.
sentences.zh: 这里有个很温馨的故事，汤姆。

sentences.en: Victor Hugo's daughter shows him in and says,
sentences.zh: 维克多·雨果的女儿领他进来并说道：

sentences.en: Papa, here is his majesty from Brazil.
sentences.zh: 爸爸，这位是来自巴西的陛下。

sentences.en: And Tom Pedro II says,
sentences.zh: 然后佩德罗二世说道：

sentences.en: My dear, there is only one majesty here, and it is Victor Hugo.
sentences.zh: 亲爱的，这里只有一个陛下，那就是维克多·雨果。

sentences.en: Oh, that's splendid.
sentences.zh: 哦，太精彩了。

sentences.en: I like him.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他。

sentences.en: Isn't that good?
sentences.zh: 这不是很棒吗？

sentences.en: I like him.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他。

sentences.en: No, I really like him.
sentences.zh: 不，我是真的很喜欢他。

sentences.en: He sources meteorites and he's polite to great French novelists.
sentences.zh: 他四处搜寻陨石，对伟大的法国小说家又很有礼貌。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Victor Hugo said to him,
sentences.zh: 维克多·雨果对他说：

sentences.en: Sire, you are a great man.
sentences.zh: 陛下，您是个伟大的人。

sentences.en: You are the grandson of Marcus Aurelius.
sentences.zh: 您是马可·奥勒留的孙子。

sentences.en: Isn't that a nice thing to hear?
sentences.zh: 听到这样的话不是很开心吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, fabulous.
sentences.zh: 对啊，太棒了。

sentences.en: Everything.
sentences.zh: 一切都好。

sentences.en: I mean, this is all very good.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这一切都很好。

sentences.en: They're all very, very, very good.
sentences.zh: 它们都非常、非常、非常好。

sentences.en: I hope it doesn't go wrong.
sentences.zh: 我希望别出什么岔子。

sentences.en: It's going to end badly, Tom.
sentences.zh: 结局会很惨的，汤姆。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: I just want to, I think, I feel like I don't want you to think, I don't want it to come as too much as a shock
sentences.zh: 我只是想，我觉得，我感觉我不想让你觉得，我不想让大家感到太震惊

sentences.en: when Don Pedro's life ends in misery, as it will.
sentences.zh: 当佩德罗的生命在痛苦中结束时，虽然事实确实如此。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 哦，不。

sentences.en: So he gets back to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 所以他回到了巴西。

sentences.en: And the Brazilians, you know, they're very displeased by all this behavior.
sentences.zh: 巴西人呢，你知道的，他们对这一系列行为感到非常不满。

sentences.en: They say, by this stage, he's grown a massive beard.
sentences.zh: 他们说，到这个时候，他已经留起了巨大的胡子。

sentences.en: He's got glasses.
sentences.zh: 他戴上了眼镜。

sentences.en: He doesn't look.
sentences.zh: 他看起来不像。

sentences.en: They're sort of puffed up, I think, a little bit with a sense of sort of national destiny.
sentences.zh: 我想他们多少有点被一种国家命运感冲昏了头脑。

sentences.en: And they think he's an unprepossessing monarch.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得他是一个毫无吸引力的君主。

sentences.en: He's too interested in books and science and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他对书籍、科学之类的事情太感兴趣了。

sentences.en: And he's unsound, as they think, on slavery, on the defense of slavery.
sentences.zh: 而且正如他们所认为的那样，他在奴隶制、在维护奴隶制的问题上态度不够坚定。

sentences.en: And so they're sort of losing enthusiasm for him.
sentences.zh: 所以他们对他逐渐失去了热情。

sentences.en: A few years go by.
sentences.zh: 几年过去了。

sentences.en: 1887, he goes on another of his trips.
sentences.zh: 1887年，他又开始了另一场旅行。

sentences.en: So he goes, this time he goes and visits Louis Pasteur, I do believe.
sentences.zh: 所以他去了，这一次他去拜访了路易·巴斯德，我相信是的。

sentences.en: And he spends a lot of time in Europe.
sentences.zh: 他在欧洲度过了很长时间。

sentences.en: He often goes under an assumed name when he's walking, when he's traveling Europe.
sentences.zh: 当他在欧洲散步、旅行时，他经常使用化名。

sentences.en: So he doesn't go as the emperor.
sentences.zh: 所以他不是以皇帝的身份出行。

sentences.en: So I think the Brazilians also think this is poor form.
sentences.zh: 所以我想巴西人也觉得这很不妥。

sentences.en: They would like him to go in splendor.
sentences.zh: 他们希望他能风风光光地出行。

sentences.en: Whereas, in fact, he goes and stays in hotels under false names and spends his time writing poeMs.
sentences.zh: 然而事实上，他却用假名去住酒店，把时间都花在写诗上。

sentences.en: And they basically think this is – and also, it's known that he's basically said to people,
sentences.zh: 他们基本上认为这——而且，众所周知，他曾对人说过：

sentences.en: I love doing this.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢这样了。

sentences.en: Left to me, I would just do this all the time.
sentences.zh: 如果由我做主，我整天就只想做这些。

sentences.en: I'd much rather live in Europe than in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我宁愿住在欧洲也不愿呆在巴西。

sentences.en: And hang around with Victor Hugo.
sentences.zh: 然后和维克多·雨果厮混在一起。

sentences.en: So meanwhile, while he's away, obviously, the issue of slavery is still there.
sentences.zh: 所以与此同时，当他不在国内时，奴隶制的问题显然依然存在。

sentences.en: Slavery has been abolished in the United States since the 1860s.
sentences.zh: 美国自19世纪60年代起就废除了奴隶制。

sentences.en: We're now in the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 我们现在已经到了19世纪80年代。

sentences.en: There's a real sense that it's on its last legs.
sentences.zh: 人们明显感觉到它已经行将就木了。

sentences.en: Not least because the age of mass immigration means that the Brazilian economy is not as dependent on slavery as it once was.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是因为大规模移民时代的到来意味着巴西经济不再像过去那样依赖奴隶制。

sentences.en: There are rising slave revolts in the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 19世纪80年代爆发了此起彼伏的奴隶起义。

sentences.en: And eventually, basically, the Brazilian government passes a law overnight, May 1888.
sentences.zh: 最终，巴西政府基本上在一夜之间通过了一项法律，即1888年5月。

sentences.en: The remaining 700,000 slaves are emancipated kind of forthwith.
sentences.zh: 剩下的70万奴隶随即获得了某种程度上的解放。

sentences.en: So end of slavery.
sentences.zh: 奴隶制就这样走到了尽头。

sentences.en: Now, the people who are really outraged about this are the coffee planters, the coffee elites of Rio and Sao Paulo.
sentences.zh: 现在，对此感到极其愤怒的人是里约热内卢和圣保罗的咖啡种植园主和咖啡精英们。

sentences.en: As far as they're concerned, they've lost their property.
sentences.zh: 在他们看来，他们的财产泡汤了。

sentences.en: They blame the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们把这怪罪于皇帝。

sentences.en: But actually, he's out of the country when it happens because he's on one of his tours.
sentences.zh: 但事实上，事情发生时他并不在国内，因为他正在外地巡游。

sentences.en: He's hanging out with Louis Pasteur.
sentences.zh: 他正跟路易·巴斯德在一起呢。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But they say it's all his fault.
sentences.zh: 但他们说这全都是他的错。

sentences.en: He hasn't stuck up for us.
sentences.zh: 他没有为我们挺身而出。

sentences.en: He's a waste of space.
sentences.zh: 他简直是个吃干饭的。

sentences.en: He's got to go.
sentences.zh: 他必须下台。

sentences.en: There's also this huge thing in Brazil of positivism.
sentences.zh: 巴西当时还有一股非常盛行的实证主义思潮。

sentences.en: You know, the sort of the late 19th century kind of the idea of science and reform and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就是19世纪末那种关于科学、改革以及诸如此类的思想。

sentences.en: That has a massive traction with the kind of Brazil, the Brazilian educated classes.
sentences.zh: 这在巴西的知识阶层中产生了巨大的影响力。

sentences.en: I guess because it's anti-clericalism.
sentences.zh: 我猜是因为它带有反教权主义色彩。

sentences.en: So, and so, and this turns against the idea of emperors, does it?
sentences.zh: 所以，然后，这开始反对君主制了，是吗？

sentences.en: Against the idea of emperors.
sentences.zh: 开始反对君主制了。

sentences.en: That kind of positivism, republicanism, secularism, this sort of beautiful new future, which just so neatly, you know, happens to align with their interests.
sentences.zh: 那种实证主义、共和主义、世俗主义，这种看似美好的新未来，恰好与他们的利益不谋而合。

sentences.en: For their interests.
sentences.zh: 为了他们自身的利益。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: So, there's all this sort of stuff about the positivism and the republicans.
sentences.zh: 所以，到处都是关于实证主义和共和主义的言论。

sentences.en: And they're all kind of meetings and conspiracies.
sentences.zh: 他们到处开会、密谋。

sentences.en: He gets back to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他回到了巴西。

sentences.en: And in 1889, on the 9th of November, 1889, he has a ball called the Ball on Fiscal Island.
sentences.zh: 在1889年，1889年11月9日，他举办了一场名为“海关岛舞会”的舞会。

sentences.en: So, this is a particular island.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个特定的岛屿。

sentences.en: And he goes, it's basically to welcome the Chilean Navy who are visiting Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他去那里，基本上是为了欢迎来访巴西的智利海军。

sentences.en: And he goes to this ball and there are all kinds of rumors going around the city about this ball.
sentences.zh: 他去参加了这个舞会，而城里到处都在流传关于这场舞会的各种谣言。

sentences.en: That there are orgies happening, that he hasn't invited sufficient numbers of bigwigs, sort of liberal-minded bigwigs and so on.
sentences.zh: 说什么那里正在举行淫乱派对，说他没有邀请足够数量的权贵，比如具自由主义倾向的权贵等等。

sentences.en: And while he's at the ball, the sort of republican agitators have a meeting with officers in the Brazilian Army.
sentences.zh: 就在他出席舞会的时候，那些共和派煽动者正与巴西陆军的军官们开会。

sentences.en: The Brazilian Army, and this is a very bizarre thing to say about an army, the Brazilian Army is a hotbed of positivism, Tom.
sentences.zh: 巴西陆军，对一个军队说这样的话真的很诡异，巴西陆军可是实证主义的温床，汤姆。

sentences.en: The officers like nothing better than an evening chatting about positivist ideas they've got from Europe.
sentences.zh: 军官们最喜欢的就是在晚上聊天时谈论他们从欧洲学来的实证主义思想。

sentences.en: So, they basically, a whole load of young officers go to this old marshal who's called Deodoro de Fonseca.
sentences.zh: 所以，一大批年轻军官去找了一位名叫德奥多罗·达·丰塞卡的老元帅。

sentences.en: They go to his house and they say, you know, in the cause of positivism and of Brazil, it's time to get rid of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们来到他家里说，为了实证主义和巴西的事业，是时候赶走皇帝了。

sentences.en: This old fool is at his party.
sentences.zh: 这个老糊涂还在开他的派对。

sentences.en: We should move against him.
sentences.zh: 我们应该对采取行动了。

sentences.en: The marshal, Deodoro de Fonseca, he sort of drags his heels a bit, but eventually agrees to do it.
sentences.zh: 元帅德奥多罗·达·丰塞卡起初有些犹豫不决，但最终还是同意了。

sentences.en: So, five days later, on the 14th of November, he rides to the army headquarters.
sentences.zh: 于是，五天后，即11月14日，他骑马前往陆军总部。

sentences.en: He, it's all a bit confused.
sentences.zh: 他，这一切都有点混乱。

sentences.en: He proclaims this coup against the emperor with the words, long live his majesty, the emperor, the imperial family and the army,
sentences.zh: 他发动了针对皇帝的政变，并喊出了这样的口号：皇帝陛下万岁，皇室万岁，军队万岁，

sentences.en: which is obviously not the ideal launch for a republican coup.
sentences.zh: 这显然不是发动一场共和政变的理想开场白。

sentences.en: But nevertheless, he says the government's got to go.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，他说政府必须下台。

sentences.en: We have a new regime and all this kind of stuff.
sentences.zh: 我们要建立新政权诸如此类的。

sentences.en: The emperor is up in his palace and he's sort of, you know, thinking about meteorites.
sentences.zh: 皇帝当时正在他的宫殿里，然后他大概在想，你知道的，陨石之类的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，完全没错。

sentences.en: He gets a telegram from the center of Rio saying there's been some kind of coup.
sentences.zh: 他收到了来自里约市中心的一封电报，说发生某种政变了。

sentences.en: And he says to his wife, oh, it's fine.
sentences.zh: 他对妻子说，哦，没事的。

sentences.en: He says, I'll go down to Rio, but when I arrive there, it'll all be over.
sentences.zh: 他说，我会去里约，但当我到达那里时，一切都结束了。

sentences.en: It's just a storm in a teacup.
sentences.zh: 这不过是大惊小怪罢了。

sentences.en: He travels by train and on the train, Tom, you'll be delighted to hear.
sentences.zh: 他坐火车出行，而在火车上，汤姆，你一定会很高兴听到。

sentences.en: He spends his time on the train.
sentences.zh: 他把时间都花在了火车上。

sentences.en: He takes it so seriously.
sentences.zh: 他对此态度极其认真。

sentences.en: He spends his time reading the latest scientific periodicals.
sentences.zh: 他把时间都用来阅读最新的科学期刊了。

sentences.en: So, he gets to the center of Rio and various sort of marquises and stuff present themselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，当他到达里约市中心时，各种侯爵之流纷纷前来拜见。

sentences.en: And they say, should we raise troops to suppress this coup?
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们要不要调集军队来镇压这场政变？

sentences.en: The emperor says, no, no, no.
sentences.zh: 皇帝说，不，不，不。

sentences.en: I know that this is nothing.
sentences.zh: 我知道这算不了什么。

sentences.en: I know the people of Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我了解巴西人民。

sentences.en: This is absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 这绝对算不上什么。

sentences.en: Then, eventually, a load of officers pitch up at the palace somewhere on the 16th of November.
sentences.zh: 然后，最终，一大群军官在11月16日左右突然闯进了宫殿。

sentences.en: And they say, actually, it is something.
sentences.zh: 他们说，其实，这还真是一回事。

sentences.en: We've decided that you and the rest of the imperial family should be banished.
sentences.zh: 我们已经决定，你和其余的皇室成员必须被流放。

sentences.en: Now, this is by no means.
sentences.zh: 现在，这绝对不是。

sentences.en: You know, we're talking about quite small groups of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们谈论的只是一小撮人。

sentences.en: This is by no means a mass uprising.
sentences.zh: 这绝不是大规模起义。

sentences.en: This isn't the French Revolution.
sentences.zh: 这不是法国大革命。

sentences.en: There are no kind of great mobs pouring through the streets because the emperor is actually pretty popular.
sentences.zh: 并没有成群结队的暴民涌上街头，因为皇帝其实挺受欢迎的。

sentences.en: But the emperor, I think partly because there's part of him that thinks this basically means a lot of time I can spend with Louis Pasteur.
sentences.zh: 但皇帝之所以这么做，我想部分原因是他内心深处觉得，这意味着他以后有大量时间可以和路易·巴斯德在一起了。

sentences.en: When they tell him this, he says, if it is so, then this will be my retirement.
sentences.zh: 当他们把这告诉他时，他说，如果真是这样，那这就是我的退休生活。

sentences.en: I've worked hard and I'm tired.
sentences.zh: 我已经努力工作，而且我很累。

sentences.en: It is time to go and reSt.
sentences.zh: 是时候离开去休息了。

sentences.en: And so, unbelievably, without raising an army to defend himself or anything like this, he says, right, let's pack our bags.
sentences.zh: 于是，难以置信的是，在没有拉起军队为自己辩护或诸如此类的情况下，他说，好吧，我们收拾行李吧。

sentences.en: In fact, the only time he kind of gets angry is when the officers come back in a day later and they say, basically, have you not packed yet?
sentences.zh: 事实上，他唯一有点生气的时刻是，军官们在一天后回来，基本上是说，你们还没收拾好行李吗？

sentences.en: You've got to go now in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 你们现在必须在半夜离开。

sentences.en: And the emperor is very cross and he shouts at them and he says, I am not an escaped slave.
sentences.zh: 皇帝非常生气，他对他们大喊大叫，并说，我不是逃跑的奴隶。

sentences.en: I will not leave in the middle of the night.
sentences.zh: 我不会在半夜离开。

sentences.en: And then he shouts, all of you are mad.
sentences.zh: 然后他大喊，你们都疯了。

sentences.en: But then he packs his bags anyway and he gets on the boat and off he goes to Europe.
sentences.zh: 但接着他还是收拾了行李，上了船，前往欧洲。

sentences.en: And that's basically the end of him.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是他的人生结局。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: So he doesn't come to a terrible end.
sentences.zh: 所以他并没有迎来可怕的结局。

sentences.en: Actually, it's quite a happy story because he said he wanted, you know, he was.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这是一个相当美满的故事，因为他说过他想要的，你知道的，他就是这样。

sentences.en: I think it's a disappointing end, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个令人失望的结局，汤姆。

sentences.en: He'd been good for Brazil.
sentences.zh: 他为巴西做过好事。

sentences.en: I thought he was going to have a horrible end in a dungeon or something.
sentences.zh: 我以为他会在地牢里或者类似的地方迎来一个可怕的结局。

sentences.en: No, no, he doesn't have an end in a dungeon.
sentences.zh: 不，不，他没有死在地牢里。

sentences.en: I'm happy about that.
sentences.zh: 我为此感到高兴。

sentences.en: And what happens to his daughter?
sentences.zh: 那么他的女儿怎么样了？

sentences.en: Well, she goes with him.
sentences.zh: 嗯，她和他一起去了。

sentences.en: Actually, she never wanted to be empress and he didn't even want her to be empress either.
sentences.zh: 事实上，她从来不想当女皇，他甚至也不想让她当女皇。

sentences.en: So this is a happy story then.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个快乐的故事。

sentences.en: This is a happy story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个快乐的故事。

sentences.en: Well, except he doesn't live very well.
sentences.zh: 嗯，只是他过得不是很好。

sentences.en: We'll come on to what happens to him.
sentences.zh: 我们接下来会讲到他的遭遇。

sentences.en: So this is 1889.
sentences.zh: 所以这是1889年。

sentences.en: I'll quote a Brazilian writer about what happened next to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我将引用一位巴西作家的话，讲述巴西接下来发生的事情。

sentences.en: So in the century after they got rid of Emperor Don Pedro II, the Brazilian Republic had 12 states of emergency, 17 institutional acts.
sentences.zh: 因此，在摆脱了佩德罗二世皇帝之后的这一个世纪里，巴西共和国经历了12次紧急状态，17次体制法令。

sentences.en: The National Congress dissolved six times, 19 military revolutions, two presidential resignations, three presidents prevented from assuming office, four presidents deposed,
sentences.zh: 国民议会解散了6次，19次军事革命，2次总统辞职，3次总统被阻止就职，4次总统被罢免，

sentences.en: seven different constitutions, four dictatorships and nine authoritarian governments.
sentences.zh: 7种不同的宪法，4个独裁政权和9个威权政府。

sentences.en: So I think it's fair to say Don Pedro II was a relative oasis of stability.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得可以说，佩德罗二世是一个相对稳定的绿洲。

sentences.en: And in fact, you ask about the slaves and what the slaves thought of him.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你问到奴隶们，以及奴隶们对他的看法。

sentences.en: He was very popular among Brazil's kind of African population and Indian population.
sentences.zh: 他在巴西的非洲裔和印第安人中非常受欢迎。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: So we did a podcast, what seems like an eternity ago, about weird wars.
sentences.zh: 所以我们曾在似乎是很久以前做过一期关于奇怪战争的播客。

sentences.en: And one of the weird wars, one of my choices was a war called The War of Canudos in the 1890s,
sentences.zh: 其中一场奇怪的战争，我的选择之一是19世纪90年代被称为卡努多斯战争的战争，

sentences.en: written about in a brilliant book called The War at the End of the World by Mario Vargas Llosa, the Peruvian noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 秘鲁小说家马里奥·巴尔加斯·略萨在一本名为《世界末日之战》的精彩著作中写到了它。

sentences.en: And this was a kind of, there was a guy called Antonio, the councillor, who led this kind of weird kind of religious commune.
sentences.zh: 这是一种，有一个叫安东尼奥的人，被称为顾问，他领导了这种奇怪的宗教公社。

sentences.en: And that appealed to former slaves.
sentences.zh: 这吸引了前奴隶们。

sentences.en: And there were thousands of them.
sentences.zh: 有成千上万的人。

sentences.en: And they fought this war in which 30,000 people died against the Brazilian government.
sentences.zh: 他们与巴西政府展开了这场战争，导致3万人丧生。

sentences.en: And part of the appeal of his kind of commune and his millenarian religious movement was that an emperor, a king, would return.
sentences.zh: 他的公社和千禧年宗教运动的吸引力的一部分是，一位皇帝，一位国王，将会归来。

sentences.en: So it was a combination of Don Pedro II and the lost king of Portugal, Sebastião, Dom Sebastiao from the 16th century.
sentences.zh: 所以这是佩德罗二世与16世纪葡萄牙失踪国王塞巴斯蒂昂的结合。

sentences.en: And this side, Don Pedro II lived on in the memory of lots of Brazilians as this kind of exiled enlightenment paragon.
sentences.zh: 从这方面来说，佩德罗二世在许多巴西人的记忆中一直作为这种流亡的启蒙楷模存在。

sentences.en: King over the water.
sentences.zh: 水上之王。

sentences.en: Yeah, the king over the water who had presided over abolition.
sentences.zh: 是的，主持了废除奴隶制的水上之王。

sentences.en: So what happened to him?
sentences.zh: 那么他后来怎么样了？

sentences.en: So he went off to Europe.
sentences.zh: 他去了欧洲。

sentences.en: It wasn't a great laugh, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是那么愉快。

sentences.en: He didn't hang out as much as he would have liked with scientists and novices because he's in very poor health.
sentences.zh: 他并没有像他希望的那样和科学家以及学者们有很多交往，因为他的健康状况很差。

sentences.en: He suffered from what I think diabetes.
sentences.zh: 他患有我认为是糖尿病的疾病。

sentences.en: Most people think he had diabetes.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为他患有糖尿病。

sentences.en: He didn't have much money because the Brazilians basically cut off all his money.
sentences.zh: 他没有多少钱，因为巴西人基本上切断了他所有的资金来源。

sentences.en: So he lived for only two years in Europe.
sentences.zh: 所以他在欧洲只生活了两年。

sentences.en: So this sort of dream of a lovely retirement.
sentences.zh: 所以这种对美好退休生活的梦想……

sentences.en: That's sad.
sentences.zh: 这真令人难过。

sentences.en: However, when he died in Paris, which he loved, of pneumonia in December 1891, the French, they're very good with dead monarchs, Tom.
sentences.zh: 然而，当他在他所热爱的巴黎于1891年12月死于肺炎时，法国人对处理已故君王很在行，汤姆。

sentences.en: Aren't they the French?
sentences.zh: 法国人不是很擅长这个吗？

sentences.en: President Macron absolutely distinguished himself.
sentences.zh: 马克龙总统绝对表现得非常出色。

sentences.en: Not always a friend of the rest is history, but he distinguished himself with his reaction to the death of the queen.
sentences.zh: 虽然他并不总是《历史其余部分》的挚友，但他在对女王去世的反应上表现得很出色。

sentences.en: So the French stage a state funeral for Don Pedro II, where his coffin was escorted by 30,000 French troops.
sentences.zh: 因此，法国人为佩德罗二世举行了国葬，他的灵柩由3万名法国军队护送。
3万人！

sentences.en: Goodness.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: And 300,000 people stood in the pouring rain to see it go.
sentences.zh: 30万人冒着倾盆大雨站在路边观看灵车驶过。

sentences.en: Well, the French do love a monarch, don't they?
sentences.zh: 嗯，法国人确实很喜欢君主，不是吗？

sentences.en: They love this.
sentences.zh: 他们太喜欢这个了。

sentences.en: There are hundreds of wreaths, and the message on the wreath that stands out, there was one wreath that said, just said simply,
sentences.zh: 有数百个花圈，其中最显眼的一个花圈上面写着，只有一个花圈上简单地写着，

sentences.en: from a Brazilian black on behalf of his race, which sort of tells you about how.
sentences.zh: 来自一个代表其种族的巴西黑人，这基本上说明了……

sentences.en: So then his coffin was taken by a train to Portugal, and he was buried alongside the other Braganza monarchs.
sentences.zh: 然后他的灵柩被火车运往葡萄牙，并与其他的布拉干萨王朝君主葬在一起。

sentences.en: Because he didn't go back to Brazil.
sentences.zh: 因为他没有回巴西。

sentences.en: To Brazil.
sentences.zh: 回巴西。

sentences.en: But, interestingly, he is pretty much regarded, I think, by a lot of ordinary Brazilians as the greatest Brazilian.
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，许多普通的巴西人都认为他是最伟大的巴西人。

sentences.en: So he wins polls and things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他在民意调查之类的评选中屡屡获胜。

sentences.en: Did they have an equivalent of the one that Salazar won in Portugal?
sentences.zh: 他们有没有类似于葡萄牙萨拉查获胜的那种评选？

sentences.en: We often talk about that.
sentences.zh: 我们经常讨论这个。

sentences.en: I don't think they did in Brazil.
sentences.zh: 我觉得巴西没有。

sentences.en: I might be wrong.
sentences.zh: 也许我记错了。

sentences.en: So there's no kind of imperial party in Brazil saying, let's-
sentences.zh: 所以巴西没有什么皇室政党说，让我们——

sentences.en: No, bring back the imperial family.
sentences.zh: 不，迎回皇室。

sentences.en: Bring back the emperor.
sentences.zh: 迎回皇帝。

sentences.en: But I think, I mean, I think Brazil is a fascinating country, obviously a great footballing history, but it'd be even more fascinating if it was an empire again.
sentences.zh: 但我的意思是，我认为巴西是一个迷人的国家，显然有着伟大的足球历史，但如果它再次成为一个帝国，将会更加迷人。

sentences.en: Don't you think, Tom?
sentences.zh: 你不这么认为吗，汤姆？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, at the moment, I'm going to pin my colors.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，此刻，我要表明我的立场。

sentences.en: Can I pin my colors to the mask?
sentences.zh: 我可以表明我的立场吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 可以。

sentences.en: I'm not a massive admirer of Bolsonaro.
sentences.zh: 我不是博索纳罗的狂热崇拜者。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: In fact, I think I would go as fast as to say he's not a friend of the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我觉得我甚至可以说他不是《历史其余部分》的朋友。

sentences.en: What about President Lula?
sentences.zh: 卢拉总统呢？

sentences.en: He's got a great name.
sentences.zh: 他有个好名字。

sentences.en: Because he was in prison, wasn't he?
sentences.zh: 因为他曾入狱，对吧？

sentences.en: He was in prison.
sentences.zh: 他曾经入狱。

sentences.en: Of the two, I would pick Lula.
sentences.zh: 在这两人中，我会选择卢拉。

sentences.en: I'll be honest with you.
sentences.zh: 老实说。

sentences.en: But given the choice of Lula, Bolsonaro, or- Or Don Pedro II, Return from the Dead.
sentences.zh: 但如果有卢拉、博索纳罗，或者——或者死而复生的佩德罗二世供你选择。

sentences.en: An emperor with an interest in meteorites, who would you go for?
sentences.zh: 一个对陨石感兴趣的皇帝，你会选谁？

sentences.en: Yeah, I'd go for the emperor.
sentences.zh: 对，我会选皇帝。

sentences.en: Well, I always-
sentences.zh: 嗯，我总是——

sentences.en: Yeah, I'm a monarchy fan.
sentences.zh: 对，我是君主制的粉丝。

sentences.en: An emperor who stages operas and gives money to historical associations.
sentences.zh: 一个制作歌剧并向历史协会捐款的皇帝。

sentences.en: I think he'd be very into dinosaurs as well, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他也会对恐龙非常感兴趣。

sentences.en: I think he's- Is he a friend of the rest of his history?
sentences.zh: 我觉得他——他算得上《历史其余部分》的朋友吗？

sentences.en: I'd like to think he is.
sentences.zh: 我愿意认为他是。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Let's enshrine him as a friend of the rest of his history.
sentences.zh: 让我们将他奉为《历史其余部分》的朋友吧。

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Well, that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这太棒了。

sentences.en: Our honor.
sentences.zh: 我们的荣幸。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 是的，这太棒了。

sentences.en: I need nothing about him at all.
sentences.zh: 我之前对他的了解为零。

sentences.en: Nothing.
sentences.zh: 一无所知。

sentences.en: So I really feel that I've educated myself here.
sentences.zh: 所以我真的觉得自己在这里受了教育。

sentences.en: You've gained a friend, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想你收获了一个朋友。

sentences.en: I've gained knowledge, and I've gained a friend.
sentences.zh: 我收获了知识，也收获了一个朋友。

sentences.en: Oh, that's lovely.
sentences.zh: 哦，太可爱了。

sentences.en: That is, you know, that can't be reckoned a waste of time.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道的，绝对不能算是浪费时间。

sentences.en: So I- If anybody says this podcast is a waste of time, I'll be very shocked.
sentences.zh: 所以如果有人说这个播客是浪费时间，我会非常震惊。

sentences.en: I hope that everyone listening, likewise, has gained a friend, perhaps, in the form of
sentences.zh: 我希望每一个收听的听众同样也收获了一个朋友，也许就是

sentences.zh: 佩德罗，并且也许学到了一些东西，就像我一样。

sentences.zh: 非常感谢大家的收听。

sentences.zh: 谢谢你，多米尼克，奉献了堪称巅峰之作的精彩表现。
